newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Straits mulls development of copper mine.
newsitem.headline: Straits mulls development of copper mine.

text.p: Straits Resources NL said on Wednesday development of the Whim Creek mine project in Western Australia could start soon, providing a substantial lift to the company's copper output.
"If we proceed with Whim Creek then cathode production will commence in the first half of 1998," Garry Lowder, chairman of Straits, told the company's annual shareholders' meeting.
"That would lift copper production attributable to Straits by 70 percent from the current 9,000 tonnes to approximately 16,000 tonnes," Lowder said.
Straits' current copper production is derived from its 60 percent-owned Girilambone copper mine in New South Wales.
Lowder said permitting for Whim Creek should be in place shortly following a series of delays.
"At that time we will make a decision about proceeding with the new mine in the light of prevailing economic conditions and our view of future copper prices and currency exchange rates," Lowder said.

Another project, Tritton, could be producing copper concentrates by early 1999 at an annual rate of 20,000 tonnes of contained metal, giving the company aggregate production from Girilambone, Whim Creek and Tritton of 26,000 tonnes a year, Lowden said.

The company also is studying development of its half-owned Maroochydore copper project in Western Australia, potentially the biggest in its portfolio and capable of producing at least 40,000 tonnes a year for 20 years, he said.
Maroochydore still requires evaluation to determine its technical and economic viability, Lowder said.
Decisions on proceeding to full feasibility studies for Tritton and Maroochydore "should be possible" in the third quarter of 1997, Lowder said.
Lowder said that at the end of the first quarter, Straits was operating above budget in terms of realised copper prices and actual operating costs.
However, reduced revenues from copper sales and project financing costs were holding back net earnings to levels below those of last year, he said.
